results.summary: This project implements a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor that reads instruction addresses and ground truth branch directions via an SPI interface. It uses latch-based memory and requires external hardware to drive 10 bits and read 5 bits. The design is based on a research paper and includes a functional simulation using a RISC-V execution log. Notable for its use of perceptron theory and a Docker-based build environment.

This design implements Karplus-Strong string synthesis with an SPI register map and I2S audio output. It requires an external I2S DAC and a 256 kHz clock to produce 8-bit signed sound samples at 16 kHz. The synthesis is based on classic papers on plucked-string algorithms. It is a complete audio synthesizer block for Tiny Tapeout.

This is a simple Wokwi design that lights up LEDs to display the letter H. It requires no external hardware beyond the standard Tiny Tapeout board. The design is minimal and likely intended for educational purposes. Documentation is sparse but the functionality is clear.

This is a slow 3-bit unsigned multiplier that computes the product over 18 clock cycles using a state machine. It requires no external hardware beyond the standard inputs and outputs. The design is area-efficient at the expense of speed. It is a clear example of a sequential arithmetic unit.

This is a UART transceiver design with 8-bit data frames and little-endian transmission. The documentation is incomplete, so the exact operation is unclear. It likely requires an external UART device for testing. The design is written in Verilog and targets a 50 MHz clock.

This design implements an 8-bit ALU using two 74181 4-bit slices, controlled via an SPI slave interface. It has been tested and works on silicon, with SPI communication verified. External hardware includes an SPI master (e.g., RP2040) and optionally a 7-segment display for debug. It is a replica of the classic 74181 ALU.

This project simulates an elevator interface on a 7-segment display, where switches select floors and the display updates accordingly. It requires an external LED display. The design is a simple state machine for educational purposes. It demonstrates floor selection and elevator movement logic.

This is a PWM module controllable via an SPI interface, allowing adjustment of duty cycle and counter value. It requires an SPI master and an oscilloscope or similar to view the PWM signal. The design includes override pins for testing. It is suitable for motor control and servo applications.

This design implements an 8-bit hyperdimensional computing classifier that computes Hamming distances to two class prototypes. It requires no external hardware and is controlled via input pins. The design is notable for using hyperdimensional computing concepts. It outputs the winning class and the calculated distance.

This is a multi-mode digital signal processor that can perform FIR filtering, multiply-accumulate, edge detection, and nonlinear compression on two 8-bit inputs. It requires no external hardware and is tested via simulation. The design is educational and demonstrates various DSP operations. It updates the output each clock cycle based on the selected mode.
